2601.13474.TOPIC_MATCH_COMMENT: Direct theory for an optimizer now used in large-scale LLM pretraining, explaining its preconditioning advantage over Adam.
2601.13474.HOTSPOT_PAPER_COMMENT: Broadly important today: End-to-end proof that spectral orthogonalization in Muon yields condition-number-independent linear convergence, decoupling the dynamics into independent spectral scalar sequences.
2601.13474.title: Preconditioning Benefits of Spectral Orthogonalization in Muon
2601.13474.abstract: The Muon optimizer, a matrix-structured algorithm that leverages spectral orthogonalization of gradients, is a milestone in the pretraining of large language models. However, the underlying mechanisms of Muon -- particularly the role of gradient orthogonalization -- remain poorly understood, with very few works providing end-to-end analyses that rigorously explain its advantages in concrete applications. We take a step by studying the effectiveness of a simplified variant of Muon through two case studies: matrix factorization, and in-context learning of linear transformers. For both problems, we prove that simplified Muon converges linearly with iteration complexities independent of the relevant condition number, provably outperforming gradient descent and Adam. Our analysis reveals that the Muon dynamics decouple into a collection of independent scalar sequences in the spectral domain, each exhibiting similar convergence behavior. Our theory formalizes the preconditioning effect induced by spectral orthogonalization, offering insight into Muon's effectiveness in these matrix optimization problems and potentially beyond.

2601.14327.COMMENT: Layer-Adaptive Expert Pruning applied during MoE pre-training, pruning underutilized experts and re-placing experts across devices by token distribution statistics; 49% pre-training efficiency gain on a 1T-parameter model.
2601.14327.TOPIC_MATCH_COMMENT: Core contribution is an expert-utilization and expert-placement algorithm inside MoE pre-training, squarely MoE training.

2601.14327.title: Yuan3.0 Ultra: A Trillion-Parameter Enterprise-Oriented MoE LLM
2601.14327.abstract: We introduce Yuan3.0 Ultra, an open-source Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model featuring 68.8B activated parameters and 1010B total parameters, specially designed to enhance performance on enterprise scenarios tasks while maintaining competitive capabilities on general purpose tasks. We propose Layer-Adaptive Expert Pruning (LAEP) algorithm designed for the pre-training stage of MoE LLMs. In contrast to previous expert pruning approaches that operate primarily in the post-training phase, the proposed algorithm enhances training efficiency by selectively pruning underutilized experts and reorganizing experts across computing devices according to token distribution statistics. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that LAEP effectively reduces model size and substantially improves pre-training efficiency. When pre-training Yuan3.0 Ultra from scratch original with 1515B parameters, this algorithm delivers a 49\% boost in pre-training efficiency and a 33.3\% reduction in total parameters, while preserving the model's outstanding multi-domain performance. On enterprise scenario benchmarks including Docmatix, ChatRAG, SummEval and MMTab, Yuan3.0 Ultra achieves leading accuracy. The model and codes are publicly available at https://github.com/Yuan-lab-LLM/Yuan3.0-Ultra.
